h: Oatcakes, Six Towns and a Few Fast Laps
p: Here's a tip from the trenches of indoor karting: turn up early. Check-in, signing the safety forms and getting your helmet sorted all take a bit of time, and nobody wants to be the one holding up the briefing while the rest of the group is itching to go. Get there with time to spare and you'll start the session relaxed rather than flustered.

Once you're out on track, the fastest drivers aren't always the bravest ones. Smooth beats wild every time. Brake in a straight line, look ahead to where you want to go rather than at the wall, and don't get dragged into a scrap on the first lap. The timing screens don't care how dramatic your overtakes were, only how quick your best lap was. Tie back long hair, leave the dangly earrings at home and expect to be a bit achy in the arms the next morning.

Stoke-on-Trent is a bit of an odd one, in a good way. It's not one town centre but six: Tunstall, Burslem, Hanley, Stoke, Fenton and Longton, all stitched together into one city. Hanley is the main shopping hub, while Burslem calls itself the Mother Town of the Potteries and is home to Port Vale. Stoke City play at the bet365 Stadium, so check the fixture list if you're driving on a match day.

If you fancy more pottery heritage, Middleport Pottery in Burslem is a working Victorian pottery by the Trent and Mersey Canal, and the Emma Bridgewater factory in Hanley is popular with fans of her spotty mugs. Before you leave, grab a Staffordshire oatcake. It's a soft, savoury pancake rolled round cheese, bacon or sausage, and locals swear by them. Proper fuel for a racing driver.
